a larger cross selling effect leads to a smaller order quantity for the competitive newsvendor model, and that the demand correlation between items has a positive effect on profit.

The main takeaway from our work is that

cross-selling can increase the order quantity of an item and the profit of a centralized newsvendor, but it can decrease the order quantity of the item and the profit in a competitive newsvendor model.
cross-selling can be used to improve profits in a centralized newsvendor ( NV ) model and reduce profits in a competitive newsvendor model.

a cross-selling effect is beneficial for both a retailer and a customer in a centralized decision-making situation but is beneficial only for a retailer and harmful for a customer in a competitive decision-making situation.
